title: Tarifa Poniente (shore effects)
assumptions: Wind from 255 deg (WSW): the Poniente is funnelled along the Strait, whose axis near Tarifa is about 70 deg, so the wind is taken along it. Waves toward 75 deg +-15 deg, periods 3.4, 4.2 and 5.3 s (about 35 km of fetch at 18 kt).
Sea floor: EMODnet about 100 m (coarse for 4 s waves), Copernicus land, OSM coast; a synthetic shelf fills gaps near the coast.
The Strait current (up to 4-5 kt against the wind) is NOT in the solver; it steepens and shortens waves, and is in the sea itself.

Sensitivity: with the scenario's plain west wind (270 deg, waves toward 90) the Spanish coast east of Tarifa lies in a long lee and the 64 deg course falls into it after about 1 km (factor 0.1 by 2.5 km). The result depends strongly on this direction, which is a guess.
Shore absorbs, no tide, no regrowth.
